window._comment: RS3 NXT. WM_CLASS survives title changes and skips the Steam launcher window.

_regions_help: anchor + dx,dy offset from that corner + fixed w,h. RS3 pins panels to edges at fixed size rather than scaling them, so this survives a window resize. Negative dx/dy measure inward from a right/bottom edge.

metrics_xp._note: XP and XP/h number rows in the Metrics panel

chat_tail._note: most recent ~15 lines of All Chat; w trimmed to end of text so the 3D world does not bleed into OCR

backpack._note: full backpack panel. grid is relative to the region's top-left; verified against a hand count of 24 occupied slots

rules.name: pack_nearly_full
rules._note: EXPERIMENTAL BASELINE ONLY. The detector is reusable, but lead_seconds, cooldown, and the cited trip/fill measurements were derived from Fishing rather than Thieving. Keep disabled until Thieving-specific inventory cadence and banking behavior are measured.

rules.name: pack_filling
rules._note: EXPERIMENTAL BASELINE ONLY. Overflow detection is reusable, but the current overflow_seconds/cooldown values and supporting measurements came from Fishing. Keep disabled until Thieving-specific inventory behavior is measured and false-positive cases are replayed.

rules.name: xp_stalled
rules._threshold_note: measured: static floor 0.001, XP tick 1.3-4.0. No mask - the Metrics panel is opaque, and a brightness mask only added antialiasing flicker.
rules._disabled_note: Superseded by fishing_stopped, which detects the same event from chat in 30s instead of 60s. Two rules firing for one spot move is just double beeping. Metrics XP is also the weaker signal: it stalls identically whether the spot moved, the client was minimised, or the panel was closed. Re-enable for a grind with no per-action chat message, where XP is the only evidence of progress.

rules.name: impling
rules.pattern: a creature is discovered while skilling|an impling (has )?appear
rules._note: Implings spawn silently and despawn; the message is easy to miss mid-grind. Rare enough to deserve its own sound - message-highlight is distinct from the warning tones used by pack_filling and xp_stalled, so it is recognisable without looking. Long timeout because the impling despawns: the popup should still be on screen when you glance over.
rules._disabled_note: Implings spawn from skilling, but the message was only verified during fishing. Re-enable once confirmed it appears while thieving - the pattern itself ('A creature is discovered while skilling') is already proven correct in live chat.

rules.name: thieving_stopped
rules.pattern: you pick the|you steal|you attempt to pick|you successfully pick
rules.suppress_pattern: can'?t carry any more|do not have any space in your inventory|not have any space
rules._note: UNVERIFIED WORDING AND TIMING. The OCR pattern is a best-effort hypothesis and stop_seconds=30 was inherited from Fishing rather than measured from a Thieving session. Keep disabled until live chat wording is captured, the action cadence is measured, and a sanitized replay fixture confirms the expected alert sequence.

rules.name: stunned
rules.pattern: you (have been |are )?stunned|fail to pick|you are caught|catches you
rules._note: Being caught stuns and damages you, and repeated stuns mean thieving has effectively stalled. UNVERIFIED WORDING - confirm against live chat. High cooldown because occasional failure is normal and expected; this should only speak up if it is worth noticing, not on every miss.

_notification_note: Rules use urgency 'normal' with an explicit timeout_ms so KDE auto-dismisses them. Setting urgency to 'critical' makes KDE keep the popup until it is closed by hand and ignore timeout_ms - only do that for an alert you must not miss.
